adjudicated.jp: 帰路を歩く。
adjudicated.en: Walking on the road home.
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says that Taichi walks home. The English is a subjectless participial fragment and literalizes the route as a road.

adjudicated.jp: 「うーむ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Mmmh-hmm."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 結局、何もない一日を過ごしてしまった。
adjudicated.en: In the end, one whole day passed with nothing done.
comments: Will make more sense like this when it's 'pastad in CCC4005 -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says he ended up spending an uneventful day. The English says the day itself passed and changes absence of events into failure to do anything.

highlights.text: one whole day passed with nothing done

adjudicated.jp: リセットがかかると知っているせいかな。
adjudicated.en: Perhaps, knowing that it will all be reset is to blame.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: どうも身が入らない。
adjudicated.en: Somehow I just wasn't into things.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: それに……学校に行っても賑やかさは感じられない。
adjudicated.en: Besides... I might have gone to school, but I cannot feel its bustling liveliness.
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says that even when he goes to school, he cannot feel any liveliness. The English turns his actual attendance into an uncertain past possibility.

highlights.text: I might have gone to school

adjudicated.jp: 世界はガラスキになっている。
adjudicated.en: The world had become almost entirely uninhabited.
adjudicated.assessment: ガラスキ says the world is largely empty or sparsely populated. 'Almost entirely uninhabited' intensifies that state, and past perfect lacks a later past anchor.

adjudicated.jp: 八人では世界とは言えない。
adjudicated.en: With eight people one cannot call it a world.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 永遠の一夏。
adjudicated.en: A single eternal Summer...
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 俺たちは、時の渦にとらわれた人類の残骸なんだろうか。
adjudicated.en: We might just be the wreckage of mankind caught in the swirl of an eddy of time.
adjudicated.assessment: 時の渦 is simply the vortex or eddy of time. The English redundantly places an eddy inside a separate swirl.

highlights.text: swirl of an eddy of time

adjudicated.jp: それとも……別の意味が。
adjudicated.en: Or perhaps... it means something else.
comments: HINT HINT HINT HINT HINT HINT HINT HINT -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 坂の途中、立ち止まる。
adjudicated.en: Midway through a hill, I come to a halt.
adjudicated.assessment: 坂の途中 means partway up or down a slope. 'Through a hill' suggests passage inside or across the landform.

adjudicated.jp: 道の脇にある雑木林。
adjudicated.en: On the side of the road there is a grove of trees.
comments: It's the one Nanaka forcefully "bumps" him into. Look below. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 思い出す。
adjudicated.en: I remember.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 思い出す……。
adjudicated.en: I remember...
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 新川豊が雑木林を眺めていた。
adjudicated.en: Shinkawa Yutaka was gazing lost at a grove of trees.
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says only that he was gazing at the grove. 'Lost' invents a mental state and is not grammatically integrated as an adverb.

adjudicated.jp: 俺はそんな新川のもとに近寄り、声をかける。
adjudicated.en: As I was drawing nearer to Shinkawa as he was, I called out to him.
comments: "as I came closer to him" + "as I was beginning to understand who he was". Shinkawa's remembering, by the way, and see below for how Taichi also does. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says that Taichi approaches Shinkawa and speaks to him. The English repeats 'as' and adds a meaningless trailing state clause.

highlights.text: As I was drawing nearer to Shinkawa as he was

adjudicated.jp: 「どうした？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "What is it?"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 新川は汗をかいていた。
adjudicated.en: Shinkawa was sweating.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 見るからに夏の汗ではない。
adjudicated.en: On closer look, that's not the sweat of the heat of Summer.
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says it is clearly not ordinary summer sweat. The English stacks two possessive prepositional phrases and capitalizes the season.

highlights.text: the sweat of the heat of Summer

adjudicated.jp: よろと後ずさる。
adjudicated.en: He staggers back, unsteady.
comments: Towards the road. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 車が来た。
adjudicated.en: A car came.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「新川！」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "SHINKAWA!"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 新川は轢かれて死んだ。それは俺のトラウマになった。
adjudicated.en: Shinkawa is struck, tumbles down and dies. That was the origin of my psychological trauma.
comments: 轢 is almost always used for "run over by a car"... but it more literally mean "be knocked down with force, as with a vehicle". Which is what happened to Shinkawa: he was pushed down stairs by Taichi during the Mansion Massacre, which is also the origin of his trauma (see CCD5001, he uses the exact same word to describe that event so there's no doubt to what he's referring to). This sentence would be perfectly true... -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: ……などということはなく、
adjudicated.en: ...and all other things of that sort that didn't happen.
comments: ...except for Shinkawa actually dying. With this denial, not a single lie was expressed in these last two sentences, and removing them would only subtract information from the story. Even though said information is pretty much impossible to see without extreme care. Oh well. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese retracts the immediately preceding imagined event: nothing like that happened. The English invents multiple other events and attaches them to an ungoverned coordination.

highlights.text: and all other things of that sort that didn't happen

adjudicated.jp: 「あ、田崎商店のデコ軽トラだ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Ah, it's the Tasaki Store's decorated company truck."
comments: Seems to mean it has a logo, but given below it's probably closer to some gaudy graffitied mess. As expectable of an ex-thug. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: 軽トラ is a kei pickup truck. The English adds that it is a company vehicle rather than merely belonging to or advertising the store.

adjudicated.jp: ド派手なソイツが、時速三十キロでゆっくりと通り過ぎていく。
adjudicated.en: That hideously flashy thing passes us by at the leisurely speed of about thirty kilometers an hour.
comments: That'd still kill you if he doesn't brake. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese calls the truck extremely flashy and gives an exact speed of thirty kilometers per hour. The English adds disgust and makes the number approximate.

adjudicated.jp: 福顔のオヤジが、俺に向かって『いつもありがと～』と手を振った。
adjudicated.en: That smiling guy waved a 'thank you for everythi～ng' towards me and waved his hand.
comments: See CCA0004. Tanaka generally avoids having unvoiced characters have actual lines, although that'll become sorta awkward at times... like here. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The driver calls out the thanks while waving. The English makes the words themselves an object he waves, then redundantly says he waves his hand.

highlights.text: waved a 'thank you for everythi～ng' towards me and waved his hand

adjudicated.jp: 俺はお得意様だから。
adjudicated.en: Because I am quite the profitable customer.
comments: Should still have money now. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: お得意様 means a valued regular customer. 'Profitable' introduces the store's economic assessment and need not follow from being a regular.

adjudicated.jp: 振り返した。
adjudicated.en: I returned the gesture.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「昭和時代のマニアックな飲料水の入荷、いつもありがとー！」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Thank you for always stocking up on soft drinks for us Showa era fanatiiics!"
comments: I'm guessing he's using 飲料水 like this, because if they said there's a specific type of drinkable water aimed at Showa era fanatics I wouldn't bat an eye in disbelief. A pox on all your houses, Japan. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese thanks the shop for stocking obscure Showa-era beverages. The English instead describes the drinkers, including Taichi, as Showa fanatics.

highlights.text: soft drinks for us Showa era fanatiiics

adjudicated.jp: アン○サ。
adjudicated.en: Am*sa
comments: This one was tough, but via the most sophisticated means of research known to mankind (chucking random katakana in the empty spot until something googles), I found it: http://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E3%82%A2%E3%83%B3%E3%83%90%E3%82%B5 -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: メ○ーイエロー。
adjudicated.en: Me**o Yello.
comments: Official rom, er, lomanization http://ameblo.jp/sunny1snowy/entry-10939170733.html -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: ネーポ○。
adjudicated.en: Neepo*.
comments: http://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E3%83%8D%E3%83%BC%E3%83%9D%E3%83%B3 -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 胡椒警部。
adjudicated.en: Inspector Pepper.
comments: ~Useless Factoid time~ the word 胡椒医者 on which this pun is based is composed of 胡椒=pepper (as in vs. salt) + 医者=MD. And it does GIS to the actual Dr. Pepper drink. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: ゲータ○ード。
adjudicated.en: Gato**de
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 伝説のソフトドリンクたち。
adjudicated.en: Legendary soft drink-tachi.
comments: Intentionally silly. This is Taichi sidetracking into weird to avoid dealing with Shinkawa, whom he long recognized even if he hasn't realized it yet at this point. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese plural suffix たち simply groups the legendary soft drinks. The English leaves it as an unexplained Japanese suffix on an English singular noun.

adjudicated.jp: 元鉄オタだからビジネスもマニアックなのだろうか。
adjudicated.en: He's a former railway otaku, so that's likely why he's equally fanatical about his business.
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese wonders whether his business is similarly niche because he used to be a train geek. It does not say he is fanatically devoted to commerce.

adjudicated.jp: どうやって入荷しているのかは知らない。
adjudicated.en: How exactly he manages to get them in stock I don't know.
comments: see CCC0009. Hmmm. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: とにかく新川は死ななかった。
adjudicated.en: Anyway, Shinkawa hadn't died.
comments: Still no lies. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese concludes the immediately imagined incident by saying Shinkawa did not die. Past perfect incorrectly places that non-event before a later past anchor.

adjudicated.jp: ピンピンしてる。
adjudicated.en: He was happy and lively.
comments: Focusing on happiness. That's what pisses him off about Shinkawa. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: ピンピンしている means that he is alive and perfectly healthy or energetic. The English adds emotional happiness.

adjudicated.jp: 「今おまえは生死の境を彷徨った。俺がこうしてがっしと腕をキャッチしなかったら、その灰色の脳細胞はアスファルトの上でグロ画像になっていただろう」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "You've wandered into the boundary between life and death right then. If I hadn't gone and caught your arm, those gray brain cells of yours would've become a Guro Scene over the asphalt."
comments: I decline responsibility to anyone who decides to GIS グロ画像 with safe search off without knowing what's gonna come up. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: グロ画像 means a graphic or gore image. The English leaves guro unexplained and capitalizes the resulting phrase as a named scene.

adjudicated.jp: 新川は震えていた。
adjudicated.en: Shinkawa was shaking.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「新川？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Shinkawa?"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「あ……悪い」
adjudicated.en: Shinkawa: "Ah... my bad."
comments: See CCA0011C. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 我に返る。
adjudicated.en: He returns to his senses.
comments: He had gotten kidnapped by paramnesia as well, and had gotten in his own flashback, perhaps even his delusional world. He acts exactly like Taichi. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「なんか……雑木林の奥とか見てたら……すげぇ気分悪くなってきて……昔から、そうなんだけどさ……わけ、わかんねぇんだけど……」
adjudicated.en: Shinkawa: "It's jus'... when I look like deep in the trees... I get this really bad feelin' and stuff... it's been like that since a long time ago... why, I totally dun'no tho..."
comments: See CCA0011C. That was 'zutto mae', this now is 昔 mukashi. It still means the same event, meaning that Taichi now is much further from those memories than he was back then. Time is passing whether he wants it or not. Maybe that's why these are sepia and those aren't... -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The rough colloquial source supports informality, but these phrases misuse 'like,' pair 'since' with a duration, and invent a malformed contraction.

highlights.text: look like deep in the trees

adjudicated.jp: 顔を手で覆って、立ちくらみに戸惑うように、しばし。
adjudicated.en: He covers his face with his hand, as if puzzled by his own dizziness, for a time.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 青い空を見あげて、喘ぐように息を吐いた。
adjudicated.en: He then looked up at the blue sky, gasping as if pained.
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says that he exhales as though gasping. The English adds pain and makes 'gasping' modify his looking up rather than the breath.

adjudicated.en: Taichi: "......"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 『俺、足が片方あんま動かなくてさ』
adjudicated.en: Shinkawa: 『Me, I can't really move one of my legs.』
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 外障だと思っていた。
adjudicated.en: I had thought he was External Damage.
comments: His Ultramarine -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: 外障 abbreviates an external disability. 'Damage' describes injury to an object, not a person's disability, and the capitalization invents an official category name.

adjudicated.jp: 群青にも少数ながら、外部障害保持者を受け入れる枠はあったから。
adjudicated.en: While in Gunjou they were a minority, there was a minimum quota of Persons Operating with External Impediments.
comments: Ugh, PC. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese says Gunjō had a small admissions category for people with external disabilities. The English changes that to a minimum quota, uses a euphemistic invented title, and romanizes the place name nonstandardly.

highlights.text: While in Gunjou they were a minority, there was a minimum quota of Persons Operating with External Impediments.

adjudicated.jp: けど豊は内障……内部障害だったのかも知れない。今にして思えば。
adjudicated.en: But could Yutaka have been Internal Damage... Operating with Internal Impediment. Maybe. In retrospect,
comments: Nickname vs. PC term -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: 内障 and 内部障害 refer to an internal disability. The English first calls the person damage, then invents a capitalized euphemistic bureaucratic label.

adjudicated.jp: 森の中。
adjudicated.en: in the middle of the woods,
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 木々に囲まれた閉鎖空間。
adjudicated.en: in a sealed space surrounded by trees,
comments: Specific term used for the Hasekura mansion and not just. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 俺も苦手だった。
adjudicated.en: I would also have felt ill at ease.
comments: Contrast the hokora. While Nanaka zubaaans him into the trees, she leads him to the hokora. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese states that Taichi was also uncomfortable in such spaces. The conditional perfect turns that fact into a hypothetical.

adjudicated.jp: 昔、心に傷を穿つ出来事があった。
adjudicated.en: A long time ago, there had been an event that had drilled a wound upon my heart.
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese metaphor says an event once gouged a wound into his heart. The English doubles past perfect and uses the wrong preposition with the literal drilling image.

highlights.text: there had been an event that had drilled a wound upon my heart

adjudicated.jp: 新川の気持ちを、だから俺は少し理解することができた。
adjudicated.en: And I could, therefore, manage to comprehend Shinkawa's feelings a little.
comments: Of course he can, since the two events coincide. The troll is just so damn obvious in retrospect. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.
